<reason>B won by making “mainly” the load-bearing comparison: hours change the alcohol input while transit mostly manages aftermath. B turned A’s concession that a night bus is not designed to stop bar fights into a burden A never met, and showed one-way “changed the address” cannot explain two-way dose-response. A’s leftover-people/sidewalk frame was vivid and a real critique of precinct-only counting, but never explained why that instrument should be the primary strategy. B’s both-and close—smaller crowd plus an exit the city already owns—was the cleaner vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s use of A’s “bus is not meant to outperform a lockout” concession, then demanding what carries “mainly” and flipping strandedness: a 4 a.m. district creates the expensive second network rather than earlier closing manufacturing the leftover.</best_rebuttal>
